summary.text: Blood pressure is the pressure of circulating blood against the walls of blood vessels, and most of it comes from the heart pumping blood.
It is usually written as the systolic pressure, the maximum during a heartbeat, over the diastolic pressure, the minimum between heartbeats.
It is one of the vital signs that healthcare professionals use to evaluate a patient's health.

facts.label: Where measured
facts.value: Most commonly in a brachial artery

facts.label: Normal resting adult
facts.value: Under 120/80 mmHg by AHA and ACC

facts.label: Daily rhythm
facts.value: Highest in early morning and evenings, lowest at night

items.prompt: A reading is 130 over 80 mmHg. What is the gap between the two numbers called?

options.label: Mean arterial pressure
Venous pressure
Pulse pressure
Normotension

items.explain: The difference between systolic and diastolic pressure is the pulse pressure; the average over a cardiac cycle is the mean arterial pressure.

items.prompt: A patient's blood pressure no longer falls overnight the way it normally does. What does losing that fall go with?

options.label: A greater future risk of cardiovascular disease
A lower risk, since the pressure stays steady
No link to later health at all
A switch from hypertension to hypotension

items.explain: Loss of the normal fall in blood pressure at night is associated with a greater future risk of cardiovascular disease.

items.prompt: A healthy adult reads just under 90/60 but feels completely fine. In practice, is the pressure treated as too low?

options.label: Yes, any reading below that mark is dangerous
No, it counts as too low only if symptoms are present
Yes, because the diagnostic standard is exact
No, because low readings are always the healthiest

items.explain: There is no accepted diagnostic standard for hypotension; pressures below 90/60 are commonly regarded as low, but in practice pressure is considered too low only if symptoms are present.

items.prompt: In many older people the gap between the top and bottom numbers widens. What is this rise attributed to?

options.label: A thicker, slower blood supply
A weaker heartbeat
A lower blood volume
Stiffer arteries

items.explain: The rise in pulse pressure with age is attributed to increased stiffness of the arteries.

items.prompt: Pressure in the right atrium of the heart is only about 5 mmHg. How does venous pressure compare with arterial pressure?

options.label: Much lower
About the same
Much higher
Too variable to compare

items.explain: Venous pressure is much lower than arterial pressure, with common values of 5 mmHg in the right atrium and 8 mmHg in the left atrium.

items.prompt: When you stand up quickly, sensors called baroreceptors help adjust your blood pressure in the short term. Through what do they act?

options.label: The kidneys, which alone adjust the pressure
The heart valves, which open and close faster
The red blood cells, which change in number
The brain, which signals nerves and hormones

items.explain: In the short term, blood pressure is regulated by baroreceptors, which act via the brain to influence the nervous system and endocrine system.
